protected_grant_rationale: All three paths match DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS' db/prepared/** entry in scripts/ods-scope.ts (lines 82-90, unchanged by this addendum) and are therefore unconditionally protected absent a resolved grant. This addendum is the authority for the registry entry; the entry in scripts/ods-scope.ts is its machine-enforced counterpart, and the two must agree exactly — which tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts asserts by reading protected_grant from docs/ops/p1a/P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json, following the pattern already established for HPO-ODS-W2-08 and HPO-ODS-W2-09. The patterns are three exact literal paths with no glob syntax, so the grant cannot reach a db/prepared sibling it does not name. NO db/prepared file is changed by THIS mission: the grant is registered in advance precisely so the successor implementation mission cannot claim retroactive authorization from the fact that a path changed.

mutation.M1: DEFERRED_TO_SUCCESSOR_MISSION. Meaningful mutation controls for the P1A node test its runtime guards — the unconditional database-CREATE revoke, the finally-guaranteed teardown and env restoration, the signal-path restoration, the order-sensitivity of the corpus proof, the fail-closed stella_0001 assertions, and the M2 check-id/count invariance under export widening. None of those exists as executable code until the successor implements the gate. They are frozen as P1A-M1 through P1A-M4 plus P1A-N4 vector (b) and P1A-N5 in docs/ops/p1a/P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json and are mandatory for the successor mission. Asserting a runtime mutation control here would be vacuous, and vacuous controls are precisely what the ODS negative-control doctrine forbids.
